predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the Cappadocian plateau around Mazaca, left to Cappadocian kings by the Seleucids

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Cappadocia, which 'became a Roman province' when Archelaus died in AD 17

ledger.x: 239: the Kingdom of Cappadocia stands independent under the Ariarathid house.
188: the southern and eastern border moves out by 49 cells.
129: Rome adds Lycaonia and Cilicia to the Ariarathid dominions after the war with Aristonicus.
110: an eastern strip passes to Pontus.
101: Cappadocia under a Pontic prince.
97: the Pontic hold ends.
95: Sulla places Ariobarzanes I on the throne, ending the Ariarathid line.
95: Mithridates contests Cappadocia.
95: Cappadocia becomes a client of Rome.
90: the Roman army arrives and the invasion is withdrawn.
90: Mithridates reinvades Cappadocia.
85: Dardanus.
77: the eastern strip returns from Pontus.
63: the eastern strip passes to the new Commagene.
36: Mark Antony installs Archelaus.
27 BC: the client relation passes from the Republic to the Empire.
27 BC: Cappadocia is a client of the Roman Empire under Archelaus (the Kingdom of Cappadocia page's infobox status runs 'Roman Republic and Roman Empire (95 BCE-17 AD)').
25 BC: Augustus gives Archelaus Cilicia Tracheia.
AD 17: the client relation ends with the annexation: the infobox runs 'Client kingdom...
AD 17: Cappadocia becomes a Roman province.

wars.name: Orophernes' usurpation
wars.outcome: Demetrius I, angered by Ariarathes V's refusal of a marriage with Laodice V, 'brought forward Orophernes'; Ariarathes fled to Rome c.

wars.name: Revolt of Aristonicus
wars.outcome: Ariarathes V 'was killed in 130, during the war of the Romans against' Aristonicus; for his help 'Lycaonia and Cilicia were added by the Romans to the dominions of his family'.

wars.name: Mithridates VI's and Tigranes' contest for Cappadocia
wars.outcome: Mithridates defeated Nicomedes 'in a series of battles' over control of Cappadocia; Rome interfered twice (95-92) and installed Ariobarzanes I (95).

wars.name: First Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Roman victory: 'Sulla finally demanded that Mithridates restore the kings of Bithynia and Cappadocia' and Mithridates 'formally accepted Sulla's terms and reconciled with Nicomedes and Ariobarzanes' at Dardanos in late summer or early autumn 85.

certainty.note: Hellenistic client-kingdom frontiers on the plateau and the Taurus, named by regions (Cataonia, Lycaonia, Cilicia), not by lines.
